BiblicalUsage: In Aramaic this word means work or business — the affairs of a province. Daniel asks that his friends be 'set over the affairs of the province of Babylon'; the accusers charge that the three 'are set over the affairs' yet serve not the king's gods; and in Ezra the same word is the work of the house of God, which ceased when the builders were stopped.
TheologicalSignificance: The three friends are faithful in the king's business and faithless to the king's gods — both at once. I believe that is the pattern for God's people in a foreign court: do the work well, serve the king honestly, and refuse the one thing that belongs to God alone.
RelatedEvents: Daniel's Resolve in Babylon; Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
